summary: Ran 32 pytest API tests (100% pass) covering leads, auth, RBAC, all public routes, invalid-slug 404s, backoffice redirect/access, and compliance-copy checks. UI tested via Playwright on the public preview URL. All pages render correctly server-side (Homepage cinematic hero, /properties with 3 prototype cards, property/area detail pages with PROTOTYPE labels, calculators with 'illustrative' disclaimer, /areas with Mapbox placeholder, backoffice dashboard + leads list + lead detail). However a CRITICAL environment/runtime bug prevents ANY client-side React hydration when the app is accessed via the preview URL — all client components stay as static HTML. Consequence: the admin-login form and Finance Enquiry form fall back to the browser's native form submission, which is a GET without a method attribute, so credentials & lead data end up in the URL query string (server logs confirm: `GET /admin-login?email=...&password=FoxyAdmin2026%21Demo`). Same for property search filters and calculator inputs — no reactivity. The same code hydrates perfectly on http://localhost:3000, confirming this is a preview/proxy/dev-server interaction bug, not a source-code bug.

ui_bugs.issue: Client component never hydrates on preview URL. Form <form onSubmit=submit> has no explicit method, so pre-hydration submit falls back to GET → password (and email) appear in URL query string and browser history (security bug). Visible in server logs as `GET /admin-login?email=...&password=FoxyAdmin2026%21Demo 200`. Works fine on localhost:3000.
ui_bugs.selector: form (no explicit method='post'), button (no explicit type)

ui_bugs.issue: Same hydration failure. Submitting the enquiry form on the preview URL fires a native GET (`GET /properties/prototype-chelsea-residence?name=...&email=...&phone=...&message=...`) instead of the intended `fetch('/api/leads', POST)`. Lead is NEVER created via the UI; only direct API POST works.
Client-side filter (Location / Bedrooms / Type / Clear) does not react to user input on preview URL — inputs have no React fiber/props attached; typing 'Chelsea' still shows all 3 prototype cards.
Illustrative disclaimer text renders (SSR) but the reactive computation of monthly repayment / LTV / yield does not update when inputs change — client-side calc code never runs on preview URL.

HMR WebSocket to wss://<preview-host>/_next/hmr returns 502 (dev-only). Not user-facing but confirms preview URL <-> next-dev connectivity is degraded. Added /app/next.config.js with allowedDevOrigins for *.preview.emergentagent.com and *.emergentcf.cloud; this silenced the 'Blocked cross-origin request' server warnings but did NOT restore hydration, so the root cause is elsewhere (likely the ingress buffering/terminating Next 16 Turbopack streaming HTML/RSC responses OR the `1167ms slow filesystem` in /app/.next/dev preventing the RSC flight payload from finishing streaming before the browser closes the read).

integration_issues.issue: Form submit doesn't call /api/auth/login from the browser; falls back to GET on /admin-login. Direct API call works (pytest verified 401/200/cookie). Login is unreachable through the intended UI on the preview URL.

SEND ENQUIRY button doesn't POST /api/leads; success screen 'ENQUIRY RECEIVED' never appears. Direct POST /api/leads works (pytest 201). Backend + persistence + activity log all verified via direct API + backoffice server-render.

issues: Design & copy look correct: dark charcoal + gold cinematic hero, headline present, no forbidden compliance phrases anywhere, prototype cards clearly labelled 'PROTOTYPE · NOT A LIVE PROPERTY', calculators show illustrative-only disclaimer, /areas shows map placeholder text.

action_items: ROOT CAUSE (main agent to solve): Client-side JS never hydrates when the FOXY Next.js 16 + React 19 + Turbopack dev app is served through the Emergent preview ingress. Investigate whether the ingress / FastAPI proxy chain is buffering or terminating Turbopack's streamed HTML/RSC payloads early. Options: (a) switch runner to `next build && next start` for the preview so it serves a production build (no streaming-dev-mode dependency), (b) disable Turbopack via `next dev --webpack`, (c) set `experimental.serverActions.allowedForwardedHosts` / RSC-related dev flags, or (d) verify ingress supports SSE/streaming `text/html; charset=utf-8` responses.

MITIGATION 1 (security-hard-fail): Even after hydration is fixed, add `method='post'` to the <form> in src/app/admin-login/page.tsx AND add `method='post'` (or a hidden action) to FinanceEnquiryForm. This ensures that if hydration ever fails again, credentials/PII do not leak into URL query strings or server access logs. Also add `type='submit'` explicitly to submit buttons.
MITIGATION 2: Consider making /admin-login use a server-action (or classic form POST to /api/auth/login) so it works even before hydration. Same for the enquiry form.
Kept /app/next.config.js addition (allowedDevOrigins) — silences the 'Blocked cross-origin' server warning; safe to keep.
Compliance copy is clean across all public pages tested (no FCA claim / number / 'Independent Mortgage Adviser' / 'Whole of Market').

Note: server logs already contain plaintext passwords in query strings from the failed UI attempts (`GET /admin-login?email=...&password=FoxyAdmin2026!Demo`). Consider log scrubbing and/or rotating the demo credential after the fix.
critical_code_review_comments: src/app/admin-login/page.tsx: <form> has no `method='post'`; <button> has no explicit `type='submit'`. Combined with `e.preventDefault()` in JS-only submit handler, any hydration failure leaks credentials to the URL. This is exploitable in ANY environment where JS fails to load (adblocker, network glitch, CSP issue).
src/components/finance/FinanceEnquiryForm.tsx: Same anti-pattern — no HTML fallback on the form; failed hydration leaks name/email/phone/message to the URL.
package.json pins `next` and `react` to `latest` — non-deterministic builds. Should be pinned to specific versions (currently resolves to next@16.3.5 / react@19.3.0).
No next.config.js was present at repo root; added minimal one with allowedDevOrigins to satisfy Next 15+ dev cross-origin gate.
Every page.tsx / component file is compressed onto a single line — dramatically hurts readability and debuggability (no per-line stack traces). Consider running prettier before commit.

success_rate.frontend: SSR 100% / client-interactivity 0% on preview URL, 100% on localhost:3000

seed_data_creation: Created 1 lead through direct POST /api/leads during pytest (name='TEST Investor <uuid>'). Also 1 lead 'TEST Investor 2ced87' persisted from earlier manual run — visible in backoffice as LEAD_CREATED activity. Two leads total in DB.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend API surface is fully green (see /app/backend/tests/test_foxy_api.py — 32 tests). Server-side rendering of every page is correct including compliance copy. The single blocker is client-side hydration on the preview URL only. When the main agent applies the fix, re-run pytest AND re-run the Playwright login/enquiry/property-filter flows against the preview URL. Two known valid signals of the fix working: (1) after `fill()` + `click('button:has-text("SIGN IN")')` on /admin-login the browser navigates to /backoffice within ~2s, and server logs show `POST /api/auth/login 200` (NOT `GET /admin-login?email=...`); (2) `Object.keys(document.querySelector('form'))[k => k.startsWith('__react')]` returns non-empty in the browser console on the preview URL.
rca of the issue: 1) Reproduction: navigate to https://dev-foxy-pull.preview.emergentagent.com/admin-login, fill email+password, click SIGN IN. Observed: URL becomes /admin-login?email=...&password=... (native GET), no /api/auth/login XHR fires, no error in console. Server access log confirms `GET /admin-login?email=...&password=FoxyAdmin2026%21Demo 200`. 2) On http://localhost:3000/admin-login the identical action calls POST /api/auth/login and redirects to /backoffice. 3) Diagnosis: on preview URL, browser downloads all 19 _next/static/chunks/*.js with 200s, but React never attaches fibers to the DOM (`Object.keys(el).filter(k=>k.startsWith('__react')) === []`). No console/page errors. 4) HMR websocket wss://<host>/_next/hmr returns 502 consistently. 5) Root cause is most likely the ingress or Next.js Turbopack streaming interaction — Turbopack dev serves the HTML in a streamed RSC-flight response, and if the reverse-proxy (ingress or /app/backend/server.py path for non-/api routes goes directly through the k8s ingress; /api goes through FastAPI) closes/buffers the stream before the client's react-server-dom-turbopack chunks resolve, hydration bails silently. 6) Mitigations: (a) run `next build && next start` for preview (production mode does not stream RSC the same way and is far more resilient to proxies); (b) force webpack instead of turbopack via `next dev --webpack`; (c) most importantly, harden the two forms by adding `method='post'` and a server-side fallback so credentials/PII never leak to URLs on hydration failure.
